text:
maria: heads-up — after the awq-v2 rollout to dedicated pool we saw 3 OOMs on worker-14 during the 15:00 load run. nvprof snapshots show lots of alloc/free churn around attention and kv-cache writeback. :frowning_face:
jon: can you paste the failure log? which model/config?
maria: model=gptx-13b-awq, batch sizes spiky between 1-8, kv_dtype=float16 in serving config. here's the tail of the worker log:
```
[2026-03-12T15:02:41Z] ERR OOM when allocating 2147483648 bytes for attention_workspace at 0x7f3a...
[2026-03-12T15:02:41Z] INFO allocator stats: total_alloc=3.4GB total_free=2.1GB largest_free=64MB
[2026-03-12T15:02:41Z] DEBUG kernel_select: selected custom_fused_attn (workspace=1.9GB) then fallback->cublas_gemm (workspace=2.1GB)
```
lee: that kernel flip is suspicious — we saw similar in canary when sequence_len spiked, the selection heuristic picks different kernels with different workspace reqs. repeated flips cause fragmentation.
anita: also check kv cache dtype path — if kv cache comes in as fp8->we upcast to fp16 for matmuls, we end up keeping both buffers for some time. logs show kv_cache_alloc=1.1GB then kv_upcast_tmp=1.1GB.
perf-bot: perf profile uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/1795/awq-oom-3 - nvprof timeline attached (look at 00:02:30-00:02:45)
jon: quick repro on bench node: sequence_len distribution [128(40%),512(50%),1024(10%)], batching heuristic tried to merge small requests and created mixed sequence batches -> big workspace from max(seq)=1024 plus per-request padding.
maria: current mitigations considered: 1) force stable kernel selection for gptx-13b-awq (prefer lower-workspace kernel) 2) reserve slab pool for kv-cache to avoid fragmentation 3) introduce workspace slicing (split attention into windows) 4) opportunistic spill-to-host for temporary upcast buffers.
lee: i prototyped workspace-slice=64MB and reserve-slab=256MB locally. results: reduced peak by ~700MB, latency +6-9ms p95, no correctness changes. repro patch:```
// runtime flags
--workspace-slice=64MB
--allocator.reserve_slab=268435456
--deferred_free_ms=400
```
anita: spill-to-host for upcast temporaries is attractive but we should be careful with pinned allocations causing CPU-side contention. maybe prefer cudaMemHostAlloc with writecombined and async memcpy.
jon: also adding a small hysteresis to kernel selection helps — only switch if new kernel reduces workspace by >20% for next N calls. that avoids flip-flop thrash.
maria: good idea. can we get a canary patch that: a) pins kernel for a model-version for 5min b) pre-reserves kv slab c) optional host-spill behind feature flag?
lee: yes i can push a canary, will add perf metrics. plan to run against synthetic spike with mixed seq lengths.
perf-bot: note: disabling dynamic kernel selection increased avg memory headroom but increased p95 latency by ~12ms. baseline vs patch results uploaded to dashboard.
anita: another wrinkle — gptq quant artifacts: AWQ uses per-channel scales that increase memory for per-token quant tables when cached — we should ensure those tables live in CPU and only transfer on demand.
maria: TL;DR: regression root = kernel-selection + batching mixing long/short seqs + kv upcast duplication triggering allocator fragmentation. Action items: @lee push canary PR with reserve-slab+slice+hysteresis + feature flag for host-spill; @jon add e2e spike test to repro; @anita audit kv dtype paths to avoid duplicate buffers; I'll coordinate rollback sched if canary fails. :thumbsup:
